title: Docker Sandboxes workspace symlinks can redirect host-side file copies
summary: A malicious sandbox can replace a shared-workspace symlink so a later user-initiated sbx cp reads or writes host files outside that workspace with the invoking user's permissions.

severity.rationale: A copy operation must encounter a workspace controlled by untrusted sandbox code. Crossing this boundary can expose host credentials or overwrite files, making the ordinary agent file-transfer workflow a high-priority exposure.

exposure: Requires untrusted sandbox code controlling a workspace symlink and a subsequent host-side copy through that workspace.

remediation.details: Upgrade to 0.51.0 or later. Until then, use a host-only path for copies instead of a host-side source or destination inside a workspace writable by untrusted sandbox code.
remediation.risk: Medium. Version 0.51.0 changes built-in agent kits and credential settings; review the release notes before updating.

verification: Confirm sbx reports 0.51.0 or later and validate trusted copy workflows.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
